extractedText: LG Display Expands AI Program Letting Non-Coders Build AppsAI Experts Coach Staff to Build Practical Skills About 450 AX Projects Identified, Backed by In-House 'HI-D CODE' Rollout Widens Beyond Manufacturing to Procurement, Finance and SalesFinance|Published 2026.09.13. 12:33:18|By Koo Kyung-woobluesquare@sedaily.com|Summary|SaveAAAA view of LG Display's exhibition booth at the 26th International Meeting on Information Display (IMID 2026), held at BEXCO in Busan from Aug. 18 to 21. Courtesy of LG DisplayLG Display (034220.KS) said on the 13th that it is expanding "AX SQUAD," a program that lets employees without technical backgrounds build their own applications, as the company speeds up an artificial intelligence transformation across the organization.Under AX SQUAD, staff in each business division identify problems or repetitive tasks in their own work as AI projects and build the solutions themselves using AI tools. AI specialists from the company's AX group serve as coaches so that all employees, including office workers outside the development and production units, can take part.The program centers on collaboration between employees who understand the work best and specialists familiar with AI technology. When a staff member pinpoints a process that needs improvement, an AI expert provides technical support to turn it into an application or a workflow automation system that can be used on the job.LG Display said the approach moves employees beyond simply using AI services, giving them experience in designing and solving problems themselves. The strategy is to build AI skills as a natural part of daily work and to spread individual success cases to other units, accelerating the company-wide transformation.LG Display will unveil FLiPP, a next-generation OLED patterning technology it developed in-house, for the first time in the world at the 26th International Meeting on Information Display (IMID 2026), held at BEXCO in Busan from Aug. 18 to 21. Courtesy of LG DisplayResults are emerging. Every organization within LG Display now takes part in AX SQUAD, and about 450 projects have been identified so far. Of those, roughly 190 have led to actual workflow automation, including a program that simplifies defect classification on the factory floor, an optical simulation tool for the development unit and an employee survey system for human resources.Applications built by employees through AX SQUAD are shared with the entire workforce through "HI-D Agent Hub," an internal app marketplace. Employees can download the apps they need and use them right away. The platform was also developed in-house by LG Display staff.The company has also been laying groundwork to spread AI use across the organization. Since last year it has run AX training programs for all employees, covering vibe coding and other tools. It also built its own vibe coding agent, "HI-D CODE," to address the difficulty of using sensitive internal company data on outside vibe coding services. Employees can use HI-D CODE to create the programs and apps they need without specialized coding knowledge."AX SQUAD is a company-wide AI innovation framework in which employees go beyond being mere AI users to identify and carry out work projects themselves," an LG Display official said. "Through work innovation involving all employees and by internalizing AI capabilities, we will further accelerate our shift into a technology-driven company."LG Display declared a full-scale AX push last year and initially focused on applying AI in its manufacturing and development organizations. From the second half of this year, it has been widening the scope to non-manufacturing areas including procurement and supply chain, customer support, finance and management, and sales and marketing.#LGDisplay#AITransformation#AXSQUAD#VibeCoding#WorkflowAutomation#EnterpriseAIOriginal reporting by Koo Kyung-woo for Seoul Economic Daily.AI-translated from Korean.
